plan: Store the input dictionary as a private deep copy at construction; to_data() returns a fresh deep copy so callers can never alias internal state.
Provide one recursive generator that walks all items in document order; total_word_count, unresolved_markers, and internal lookups all reuse it.
Count note words by first stripping marker tokens [[?identifier]] (replacing them with a space) and then counting \b\w+\b matches; add each reference's declared word_count.
Collect unresolved identifiers into a set from both note-text markers and reference 'unresolved' lists, then return them sorted lexicographically.
Render the outline by emitting the workspace title, then recursing through items with indent '  ' * depth and line format '<kind>: <title>', where the workspace's direct items are depth 1.

Implement move() as validate-then-mutate: check id types, locate the item and its parent list, resolve the destination ('workspace' literal or a section/group id), reject non-containers, reject moving an item into itself or any of its descendants (subtree id search), and range-check the insertion index against the destination's current length — all before touching the tree, so any ValueError leaves to_data() exactly unchanged.
Perform the mutation as delete-from-parent followed by append/insert of the same item object, preserving the item and its entire subtree.
mechanisms: Deep-copy isolation at both construction (Workspace(data)) and export (to_data)
Single document-order recursive walker shared by all aggregate queries
Regex marker stripping before regex word counting for notes
Set-based accumulation with sorted output for unresolved markers
Depth-tracked recursive outline renderer with two-space indentation
Full precondition validation before mutation in move() (type, existence, container, cycle, index checks) guaranteeing atomic failure
Subtree id search to enforce the no-self/no-descendant containment rule
